title: fix(desktop): a cancelled or failed record start never strands the app
body:
> **Stacks on #391.** This branch is based on `fix/countdown-wait-for-shade` and targets `main`. Merge #391 first; until then this PR's diff also shows #391's commit (`55588d94`). Review the five commits after it.

## Summary

Release blocker: on a single-display MacBook, starting a Screen recording and cancelling it left the app "stuck" — main window back but with grey traffic lights and not responding to the keyboard. An audit found five ways a cancelled or failed start could strand the app. This PR fixes all five, one commit each, each with a regression test that fails without its fix (checked by reverting the source and re-running).

The owner's case is most likely **D1**.

## Defects

### D1 — Cancelled region countdown brings the window back unfocused (regression from record modes)
- **Trigger:** cancel during the 3-2-1 drawn on the overlay's region (Esc, tray "Cancel countdown", ⌃⌘S) after another app became active. The shade lets clicks through, so clicking anywhere during the countdown activates the app below it.
- **Left behind:** the hub's abandon path called only `onAbandoned` = `showMainWindow` (`show()` + `focus()`). It never called `app.focus({ steal: true })` or `applyDockPolicy()`, unlike the stop restore. The window came back without the app being activated: grey traffic lights, no key focus. The Dock entry that hiding the window had dropped was not restored either.
- **Fix:** `recording-hub.ts` — new `revealAbandoned()` runs the caller's reveal, then the same Dock re-assert + `app.focus({ steal: true })` as `applyStopWindowState`. Used for every abandon (cancel, failure, TTL expiry, nothing to draw on).
- **Test:** `recording-hub.test.ts` "a cancelled countdown brings the app back as a stop does…".

### D2 — A cancel during "starting" waited on an engine that might never come (pre-existing)
- **Trigger:** Stop / tray / ⌃⌘S while the take is acquiring, when one of its awaits hangs (screen or mic `getUserMedia`, compositor `play()`, `output.start()`, `recordingCreate`).
- **Left behind:** the cancel only set a flag that was read after `startEngine` settled. If it never settled: main window hidden, bar frozen at 0:00, Stop dead, every new start refused.
- **Fix:** `recorder-store.ts` — the start in flight is tracked as a `PendingStart`. A cancel during "starting" now drops it immediately: the store goes idle and `recordingStop` restores the window. Anything the dropped start acquires later is released by `discardStart`: the engine is stopped when it resolves, the session is aborted once main has created it, and late chunks are not written. The start also has a 10 s limit (`START_TIMEOUT_MS`). Past it, the start fails through the existing start-failure path (error toast, abort, window restored).
- **Tests:** `recorder-store.test.ts` — "cancelling during the 'starting' gap restores the app at once…", "a cancel during 'starting' works even when the engine never settles", "fails a start that hangs, restores the app, and releases an engine that resolves late".

### D3 — The first-frame cap only moved the hang to the compositor
- **Trigger:** a capture track that never delivers a frame, on a MacBook. There the compositor always runs, because the Retina frame is downscaled.
- **Left behind:** `measureFrameSize` gave up after 1.5 s, but the compositor's own `video.play()` (and the thumbnail's) had no limit, so `startEngine` hung. The result was the D2 state.
- **Fix:** a shared `playWithin()` in `frame-size.ts`, used by frame sizing, the compositor and the thumbnail. On timeout the compositor rejects, so the start fails cleanly, and the engine stops the screen capture it acquired. The thumbnail falls back to no poster.
- **Test:** `recorder-engine.no-frame.test.ts`. It uses the real compositor; `play()` never resolves; `startEngine` must reject and stop the screen track.

### D4 — Control bar shown after the take already stopped (pre-existing)
- **Trigger:** a stop, or a failed start that restores, landing before `desktopCapturer.getSources()` resolves (100–500 ms after `recordingStart`).
- **Left behind:** the lookup's `.then` called `bar.show()` with no check. The always-on-top bar stayed up over nothing.
- **Fix:** `recording-hub.ts` — the lookup returns early if the take is no longer active, the same check the shade branch already had.
- **Test:** `recording-hub.test.ts` "a stop that lands before the source lookup resolves never brings the bar up".

### D5 — An input that throws at countdown end left the store in "starting"
- **Trigger:** `resolveInput()` throws when the countdown ends (for example, no source selected).
- **Left behind:** the status had already switched to "starting", so `beginEngine` never ran. The shade spinner stayed up, Esc stayed registered system-wide, the tray still showed a pending take, the window stayed hidden and new starts were refused.
- **Fix:** `recorder-store.ts` — the input is resolved while the store is still "counting". If it throws, the store reports the start error and goes back to idle. Main reads that as an abandoned countdown and restores the app, which with D1 now includes activating it.
- **Test:** `recorder-store.test.ts` "goes back to idle, never 'starting', when the take's input cannot be resolved".

## Not changed: Esc during the "starting" spinner

Esc is still released when `recordingStart` arrives, and that happens a moment after "starting", because the window is hidden before streams are acquired. So during acquisition Esc does nothing, even though the countdown hint mentions it. Keeping Esc until the engine is actually recording would need a new "engine running" signal from the recorder to main. That is more than this fix should take on. The other cancel routes (bar Stop, tray, ⌃⌘S) do work during acquisition now (D2), and a start that hangs fails on its own after 10 s.

## Verification

- `bun run check-types` — passes.
- `bunx oxlint src` — 0 errors. The 17 warnings are pre-existing and none are in the changed files.
- `bunx vitest run` (apps/kaipu-record) — 282 files, 2584 tests pass.
- Each new test was run with its fix reverted and failed.

## Manual QA (owner's MacBook, single display, Record page → Screen)

1. Start → during 3-2-1 click into another app (Finder or a browser) → press **Esc**. The main window comes back focused (coloured traffic lights, typing works), and Kaipu is in the Dock and Cmd+Tab.
2. Same, but cancel with the **tray → Cancel countdown**.
3. Same, but cancel with **⌃⌘S**.
4. Start, and press **Stop** (bar or ⌃⌘S) within the first second after the countdown ends. The window comes back, no control bar is left on screen, and no recording appears in the library. Starting again works.
5. Sanity: a normal start → record a few seconds → stop still saves and opens the recording.
